newsitem.title: USA: Continental earnings fall; profits went to buy new planes.
newsitem.headline: Continental earnings fall; profits went to buy new planes.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. Wednesday reported sharply lower profits for the third quarter, blaming the downturn on the cost of updating its fleet of planes.

The nation's fifth-largest airline said it earned $18 million, or 25 cents a share, in the latest quarter, down from year-ago earnings of $111 million, or $1.34 a share. Revenues rose to $1.76 billion from $1.5 billion.
Continental said excluding special expenses, it had operating income of $101 million, or $1.28 a share, which the company said was in line with Wall Street's expectations.
The airline said it took a charge of $77 million in the third quarter to cover the cost of replacing old aircraft with new planes and a $6 million charge for early debt retirement.
The company said it prepaid $324 million of debt, which should save $6 million in annual interest payments in the first year.
Continental's class A shares were off 12.5 cents at $24.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
